```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, comment = "#>", warning = FALSE,
                      message = FALSE)

# The analysis lives in portfolio.R; this report reads its results rather than
# re-implementing them, so the document cannot drift from the script. Knitting
# sets the working directory to this file's folder, which is what portfolio.R
# expects.
invisible(capture.output(source("portfolio.R")))

pct <- function(x, d = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), x * 100)
```

## (a)

Monthly adjusted close prices were downloaded from Yahoo Finance through the
Shiny app, covering January 2017 through December 2021. Five sectors, six
stocks each.

```{r sectors}
tk  <- setdiff(colnames(ret), "^GSPC")
sec <- c("Technology", "Communication Services", "Financial Services",
         "Consumer Cyclical", "Healthcare")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Sector  = sec,
  Tickers = vapply(1:5, function(i)
    paste(tk[((i - 1) * 6 + 1):(i * 6)], collapse = ", "), character(1))
))
```

`^GSPC` is carried alongside as the market index as asked for, for 31 assets in total.

## (b)

Adjusted close prices are converted to simple (arithmetic) monthly returns:

$$R_t = \frac{P_t - P_{t-1}}{P_{t-1}} = \frac{P_t}{P_{t-1}} - 1$$

```{r ret-dim}
cat(sprintf("prices : %d months x %d assets\n", nrow(P), ncol(P)))
cat(sprintf("returns: %d months x %d assets   (%s to %s)\n",
            nrow(ret), ncol(ret), format(dates[2]), format(dates[length(dates)])))
```

The first month is lost to differencing, so we have
`r nrow(ret)` monthly returns.

```{r ret-head}
knitr::kable(round(ret[1:4, 1:7], 4), caption = "First four rows (first 7 assets)")
```

## (c)

```{r stats}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Asset = names(means),
             `Mean (%)` = round(means * 100, 3),
             `Std. dev. (%)` = round(stdev * 100, 3),
             check.names = FALSE),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = "All 31 assets, monthly")
```

The variance-covariance matrix is `r nrow(covmat)` × `r ncol(covmat)`; the top-left
corner is shown below. The full matrix is too wide to display at a readable size,
and is computed in the appendix code.

```{r covmat}
knitr::kable(signif(covmat[1:6, 1:6], 3))
```

## (d)

```{r plot, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("risk_return.png")
```

Parts (e) and (f) are marked on the same plot.

## (e)

Equal weights across the 30 stocks, $w_i = 1/30$. Portfolio mean is
$\bar{R}_p = w'\bar{R}$ and standard deviation is $\sigma_p = \sqrt{w'\Sigma w}$.

```{r equal}
cat(sprintf("mean = %.4f  (%s per month)\n  sd = %.4f  (%s)\n",
            mu_eq, pct(mu_eq), sd_eq, pct(sd_eq)))
```

## (f)

The weights of the minimum risk portfolio are

$$x = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}}{\mathbf{1}'\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}}$$

where $\Sigma$ is the 30 × 30 variance-covariance matrix of the 30 stocks and
$\mathbf{1}$ is a 30 × 1 vector of ones.

```{r minrisk}
cat(sprintf("mean = %.4f  (%s per month)\n  sd = %.4f  (%s)\n",
            mu_min, pct(mu_min), sd_min, pct(sd_min)))
cat(sprintf("\nweights sum to %.4f, range %.3f to %.3f, %d short positions\n",
            sum(x_min), min(x_min), max(x_min), sum(x_min < 0)))
```

```{r weights}
w <- sort(x_min[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Stock = names(w)[c(1:5, 26:30)],
  Weight = round(unname(w)[c(1:5, 26:30)], 4),
  row.names = NULL), caption = "Five largest and five smallest weights")
```
